statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low with equity index futures closed and no live NQ price path available, while Stress stays elevated on multi-decade-high long-end yields, elevated oil and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz conflict.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the Sunday 22:00Z CME futures reopen into the early Asian hours, where accumulated weekend headline risk would first be priced. headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail low into the Sunday futures reopen; Stress elevated on multi-decade-high long-end yields
body: Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so no live NQ price path exists at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects absent path risk rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, mid-range inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range and about half a percent below its 30,770.63 52-week high, with the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72 and VIX down 5.11% to 14.87. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no repeated failure of retracement, which is the evidence the Tail contract requires before a higher reading is justified. The background is nonetheless demanding. A second week of global bond selloff carried the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.18% at Friday's close after an intraweek 5.225% print, the highest since 2007, with the 30-year near 5.502%, the highest since 2004, while market pricing implied roughly two-thirds odds of a 25 basis point Fed hike at the next meeting and New York Fed President Williams called another year-end hike reasonable. University of Michigan's final September sentiment fell to a four-month low of 48.1 with inflation expectations rising sharply. WTI ended at $92.41 and Brent near $104.32, both well above normal levels and both 7.5% and marginally changed respectively on the week, with an unresolved Strait of Hormuz conflict, a Houthi missile barrage on Saudi Arabia earlier in the week and, against that, direct US-Iran talks in New York that pushed oil lower on Friday. Weekly leadership was narrow, with the Nasdaq up about 2.1% while the Russell 2000 fell about 0.8%. Those conditions describe a difficult, potentially high-drawdown environment that can still mean-revert, which maps to elevated Stress rather than to Tail. The shared Finviz context read this run was stale at roughly six and a half hours old and partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was not used to establish current structure. Confidence is held in the solid band: index levels, yields, oil, VIX, the Iran situation and the coming week's US calendar were verified from primary and reputable current sources this run, but the live NQ price path is unavailable until futures reopen at 22:00Z.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were left unchanged. Tail drifted down from 8 to 6 across the period while Stress rose from 46 to 57 and Confidence decayed from 84 to 68, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates and oil backdrop. The mapped state remained EA_ON throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours. Risk is held near the closed-period baseline through Sunday, lifts into a published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures reopen where accumulated weekend headline risk is first priced, and then decays through the Asian and European hours on the assumption that reopen pricing is absorbed with normal two-way discovery. Confidence improves after the reopen as a live NQ price path becomes observable again. Stress stays elevated throughout on unresolved long-end yield pressure, elevated oil and Strait of Hormuz risk ahead of a data-heavy week that runs from JOLTS and consumer confidence on Sep 29 through August Core PCE on Sep 30, ISM Manufacturing on Oct 1 and September payrolls on Oct 2.
